blogs.title: From Predictor to Architect: Why LLMs are the Newest Feature Engineers
blogs.description: Most people use LLMs to get answers directly, but this post explores a smarter way: using them as 'architects.' We explain how FeatLLM shifts the LLM's role from predicting every single row of data (which is slow and expensive) to generating the underlying 'rules' of a dataset, allowing for lightning-fast predictions using simple traditional models.

blogs.title: Small Data, Big Insights: How to Train AI When You Only Have a Handful of Examples
blogs.description: In industries like healthcare and finance, getting labeled data is expensive and difficult. This post breaks down the 'few-shot learning' concept and explains how FeatLLM leverages the 'prior knowledge' already inside LLMs to make highly accurate predictions even when you only have a tiny amount of training data.

blogs.title: Beating the Token Limit: How to Feed Massive Tables into an LLM
blogs.description: One of the biggest hurdles in AI today is 'context window' limits—you can't just dump a 100-column spreadsheet into a prompt. This post dives into the technical cleverness of the paper's 'bagging' and 'ensemble' approach, showing how the researchers managed to scale LLM intelligence to massive, complex datasets without hitting the wall.

blogs.title: Teaching AI to Filter Out Noise: The Secret to Robust Data Science
blogs.description: AI often falls for 'spurious correlations'—patterns that look real but are actually meaningless. This post explains the two-step reasoning process used in FeatLLM: first, the AI uses its general knowledge to understand the problem, and second, it uses specific examples to build rules. We'll show how this prevents the model from getting distracted by irrelevant data.
